lines.text: You probably didn't know this about money.
lines.tts: You probably didn't know this about money.
A one hundred dollar bill is worth one hundred dollars…

lines.text: but it doesn't cost anywhere near $100 to make.
lines.tts: but it doesn't cost anywhere near one hundred dollars to make.

lines.text: The government isn't putting $100 worth of material into every $100 bill.
lines.tts: The government isn't putting one hundred dollars worth of material into every one hundred dollar bill.

lines.text: It's basically a specially designed piece of paper with ink, security features, and advanced printing.
lines.tts: It's basically a specially designed piece of paper with ink, security features, and advanced printing.

lines.text: What gives it its $100 value isn't the material it's made from.
lines.tts: What gives it its one hundred dollar value isn't the material it's made from.

lines.text: It's the fact that people, businesses, banks, and governments agree to accept it as $100.
lines.tts: It's the fact that people, businesses, banks, and governments agree to accept it as one hundred dollars.

lines.text: The same idea works with a $1 bill.
lines.tts: The same idea works with a one dollar bill.

lines.text: The paper itself has very little value.
lines.tts: The paper itself has very little value.

lines.text: But the number printed on it changes what you can buy with it.
lines.tts: But the number printed on it changes what you can buy with it.

lines.text: So when you're holding a $100 bill…
lines.tts: So when you're holding a one hundred dollar bill…

lines.text: you're not really holding $100 worth of paper.
lines.tts: you're not really holding one hundred dollars worth of paper.

lines.text: You're holding something that society has agreed is worth $100.
lines.tts: You're holding something that society has agreed is worth one hundred dollars.

lines.text: And that's one of the strangest things about money.
